summary: In Greek mythology, Hippothous is son of Lethus (himself son of Teutamus), a Pelasgian leader from Larisa who co-commands the Pelasgian contingent at Troy with his brother Pylaeus. Homer has Ajax Telamonius kill him as he drags Patroclus' corpse by the foot to please Hector. Distinct from Priam's son Hippothous and from the Attic or Arcadian Hippothoi.

sections.heading: Pelasgian captain
paragraphs: In the Catalogue of Ships Homer sets Hippothous and Pylaeus, sons of Pelasgian Lethus son of Teutamus, over the spear-fighting Pelasgi who dwelt in deep-soiled Larisa. Apollodorus' epitome likewise lists him among Troy's allies.
During the fight over Patroclus' body he tries to drag the corpse away for Hector's sake; Telamonian Ajax strikes him down and ends the attempt.

sections.heading: Many Hippothoi
paragraphs: Wikipedia enumerates several men of the name: an Aegyptid bridegroom, Poseidon's son by Alope (Hippothoon), an Arcadian Calydonian hunter, a son of Hippocoön, and a son of Priam.
The atlas id hippothous-pelasgian is strictly the Larisan ally of Troy; hippothous-trojan and other nodes hold the Priamid and remaining homonyms.
